analyses.name: Bank of America Corporation
analyses.verdict: The cleanest large-cap breakout in the scan — half a percent from its 52-week high with relative strength also at its high, at 12.1x forward earnings.

financials.summary: Net interest income was the engine of the year. The deposit repricing pressure that defined 2023-24 finally abated, and because the securities book kept rolling off at low yields into materially higher reinvestment rates, the net interest margin expanded through every quarter. Fee businesses did their part: investment banking recovered with the capital-markets cycle and wealth management fees compounded on higher asset values. Credit costs stayed benign — card charge-offs normalised rather than deteriorated, and commercial provisioning was driven by reserve-building on office real estate rather than by realised losses. Expense discipline held, so the operating leverage was genuine: revenue growth of roughly 17% converted into EPS growth of roughly 34%, with the buyback amplifying the per-share figure. The one blemish sits in accumulated other comprehensive income, where the held-to-maturity portfolio carries substantial unrealised losses that grow whenever the long end of the curve sells off — which is exactly what is happening now with the 30-year at a 19-year high.

EPS +34.1% — roughly double the revenue growth rate, showing real operating leverage
Forward P/E of 12.1x — a low-teens multiple for a mid-thirties earnings grower
Net interest margin expanded across the year as low-yield securities rolled into higher reinvestment rates
Credit costs normalised rather than deteriorated; card losses stayed inside historical ranges
Substantial buyback activity amplified per-share earnings
Unrealised losses on the held-to-maturity book remain the balance-sheet overhang

accomplishments: Restored net interest income growth after two years of deposit-cost compression
Grew digital and mobile primary-relationship households to record levels, lowering deposit acquisition cost
Rebuilt investment-banking share through the capital-markets recovery
Passed regulatory stress testing with capital headroom sufficient to sustain both dividend growth and buybacks
Expanded consumer lending partnerships internationally, including the Jio credit tie-up in India

The advance has been notable for how orderly it was — volume through the final consolidation ran at only 0.75x average, which is the signature of accumulation rather than chasing. analyses.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: RSI 58 while sitting 0.6% below the 52-week high — the most un-extended near-high setup among the money-centre banks, with the sector's best balance sheet.

financials.summary: The most complete year among the large banks, because every engine contributed at once. Revenue grew roughly 30% — an extraordinary figure for an institution this size — driven by net interest income on a repricing asset base, a genuine recovery in investment-banking fees, record trading revenue through a volatile rate environment, and asset and wealth management fees compounding on higher market levels. Credit was the quiet story: provisions built modestly against card growth rather than against deterioration, and the reserve position entering the current period is conservative. Expenses grew, reflecting continued technology investment and compensation in the capital-markets businesses, but revenue outpaced them comfortably, producing roughly 47% EPS growth. The balance sheet is the strategic asset — the excess capital position gives management the option to lean into a credit dislocation rather than to defend against one, which is precisely the optionality that commands a premium multiple in the current environment of 19-year-high long-end yields.

analyses.name: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
analyses.verdict: The cheapest high-conviction name in the scan at 8.4x forward earnings — a way to own the financials leadership without the oil-and-rates correlation that dominates the rest of the tape.

financials.summary: A year in which the two things that matter for a life reinsurer both went right at once. Premium growth of roughly 18% came from a hard pricing environment — cedants continued to offload longevity and mortality risk, and RGA was able to write that business at attractive terms rather than competing on price. Simultaneously, the investment portfolio — the second, quieter half of the earnings engine — benefited materially from higher reinvestment yields, because a reinsurer's float gets reinvested continuously and rising long-end rates are a straightforward tailwind rather than the mark-to-market problem they represent for banks. Mortality experience normalised toward assumptions after several volatile years, which removed the drag that had suppressed reported earnings. The combination produced roughly 160% EPS growth, flattered by the low prior-year base but real in direction. Reserve adequacy and the assumption set behind the long-duration liability book remain the least transparent part of the story, as they are for every reinsurer.

analyses.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
analyses.verdict: The purest listed expression of the Hormuz disruption — 348% EPS growth at 11.1x forward — but 23% above its 50-day, so the setup is excellent and the entry is late.

financials.summary: A refining year that will be remembered as exceptional. Crack spreads — the margin between crude input and refined product output — widened dramatically as global product inventories drew down and refining capacity remained structurally tight after a decade of closures. Because refining is a spread business with largely fixed operating costs, that margin expansion flowed to the bottom line with enormous leverage: revenue grew roughly 54% while EPS grew roughly 348%. The midstream segment provided a fee-based earnings floor that is worth more than the market typically credits, insulating a portion of cash flow from the commodity swing. Management directed the resulting free cash flow overwhelmingly to buybacks, materially shrinking the share count and amplifying per-share figures. The critical caveat for anyone reading these numbers as a run rate: these are peak-cycle refining margins. The 11.1x forward multiple is calculated on earnings that assume conditions persisting, and refining has never been a business where peak margins persist indefinitely.

analyses.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The widest gap between fundamentals and price in the scan — 345.7% revenue growth for 6.5x forward earnings, sitting 19.9% below its high with TradingView on STRONG BUY.

financials.summary: One of the most extreme cyclical recoveries in semiconductor history. The memory market moved from deep oversupply to genuine scarcity, and because memory is a commodity with enormous operating leverage, the swing was violent in the right direction: revenue grew roughly 346% and EPS grew roughly 1,369% off a loss-making base. The driver was high-bandwidth memory, where every AI accelerator requires multiple HBM stacks and where qualification cycles are long enough that supply cannot respond quickly to demand. Micron sold out its HBM capacity well in advance, which converted a spot-price business into something closer to contracted revenue for that segment. Gross margins expanded dramatically as pricing recovered against a largely fixed cost base. Capital expenditure remains enormous — this is a business that must spend through the cycle to hold technology parity — and that spending is what makes the 6.5x forward multiple both tempting and rational: the market is pricing the near-certainty that the cycle eventually turns down again.

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: The AI-infrastructure trade that is actually working while the semis repair — 87.5% revenue growth, relative strength at its high, 0.7% from the 52-week high.

financials.summary: A year defined entirely by AI server demand. Revenue grew roughly 88% as the infrastructure solutions group converted an enormous AI server backlog into shipments, and EPS grew roughly 283% as that volume leveraged a largely fixed operating cost base. The critical nuance that the headline growth obscures is margin structure: AI servers are substantially lower-margin than Dell's traditional enterprise hardware, because much of the bill of materials is bought-in GPU content on which Dell earns an integration margin rather than a component margin. So revenue growth materially overstates the underlying profit-pool growth, and the mix shift is dilutive to percentage margins even as it is strongly accretive to absolute dollars. The traditional client solutions business — PCs — remained the stable, cash-generative counterweight. Free cash flow funded both debt reduction and shareholder returns. At 21.7x forward the market is paying a moderate multiple, which seems to reflect appropriate scepticism about the durability of AI server margins rather than doubt about the demand.

analyses.verdict: The one group that gets structurally better from the exact headlines threatening the rest of the tape — 0.2% from its high on only 0.55x volume.

financials.summary: A year in which the commercial aerospace aftermarket and the defence backlog both worked. Revenue grew roughly 15%, with the commercial aftermarket the highest-quality contributor — spare parts and maintenance on installed engines carry far better margins than original equipment, and record global flight hours drove that volume. On the defence side, elevated geopolitical tension translated into a growing backlog across missiles, air defence and precision munitions, though defence revenue recognition lags order intake by years, so the backlog is a forward indicator rather than a current earnings driver. EPS grew roughly 29%, ahead of revenue, reflecting the aftermarket mix benefit and the absence of the large one-off programme charges that had disrupted prior years. Free cash flow supported both the dividend and debt reduction. At 28.2x forward the multiple is full for a defence prime — the market is paying for the aftermarket annuity and the geopolitical backlog visibility rather than for the current earnings level.

analyses.name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A way to own AI datacenter demand through contracted leases rather than chip order books — 29.9% revenue growth, 1.2% from the high, RSI 56.

financials.summary: A year in which datacenter leasing became a genuinely capacity-constrained business. Revenue grew roughly 30% as AI training and inference workloads absorbed available capacity and pricing power shifted decisively to landlords — releasing spreads on expiring leases turned strongly positive, which is the single most important economic indicator for a REIT of this type. The binding constraint on growth is no longer tenant demand but power availability: securing grid interconnection and generation capacity has become the competitive moat, and the multi-year lead times on power mean the supply response to current demand is structurally slow. That dynamic is what justifies a premium multiple. The reported earnings line is unhelpful — EPS growth was negative at -58.7% and the forward P/E of 68.5x is nearly meaningless, because REIT accounting runs large depreciation charges against properties that are appreciating; funds from operations is the correct earnings metric. The genuine financial vulnerability is the balance sheet: this is a capital-intensive development business carrying meaningful leverage at precisely the moment the 30-year Treasury yield has reached a 19-year high.

analyses.name: Amgen Inc.
analyses.verdict: 0.6% from its 52-week high at 17.2x forward with 64.9% EPS growth, and TradingView independently rates it STRONG BUY — its top tier.

financials.summary: A year where modest top-line growth translated into dramatic earnings growth. Revenue grew roughly 10%, driven by the newer product portfolio offsetting erosion in mature franchises facing biosimilar competition — the perennial structural challenge for a company of this vintage. EPS grew roughly 65%, and the gap between those two figures is the story: operating discipline, the annualisation of acquisition synergies, lower amortisation and a reduced share count all amplified a single-digit revenue increase into a mid-sixties earnings increase. That is high-quality in the sense that it is real cash earnings, but it is not repeatable indefinitely — cost synergies are a finite resource, and sustaining this earnings trajectory eventually requires the revenue line to accelerate. Free cash flow remained robust and supported both the dividend and continued debt reduction following prior acquisition activity. The obesity and metabolic pipeline is where the market's forward expectations are concentrated, and those expectations are high.

analyses.name: SpaceX (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.)
analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING — judge the business, not the chart: a launch monopoly with a Starlink subscription annuity, growing revenue 91.9%, now 33.8% below its post-IPO high as float euphoria unwinds.

financials.period: FY2025 (last full fiscal year disclosed ahead of listing)
financials.summary: Two distinct businesses in one company, and the market is still deciding how to value the combination. The launch business is the dominant global provider of orbital lift, and its economics rest on booster reusability, which has driven cost per kilogram to orbit far below any competitor — that is a genuine and durable structural advantage rather than a temporary lead. The second business, Starlink, has become the more interesting one financially: a satellite broadband subscription service with recurring monthly revenue, which is a fundamentally different and higher-quality revenue profile than lumpy launch contracts, and it is what drove the roughly 92% revenue growth into the listing. The capital intensity of both businesses is extreme — constellation replenishment is a permanent ongoing cost, not a one-time build — and free cash flow generation is therefore the key thing to watch rather than revenue growth. As a very recent listing, the disclosure history is thin and the reported figures deserve more caution than those of an established filer. The 88.1x forward multiple prices substantial execution success.

Booster reusability delivers a structural cost-per-kilogram advantage over every competitor

Forward P/E of 88.1x prices in sustained flawless execution

Scaled Starlink into a genuine consumer and enterprise broadband subscription business

journey_52w.summary: There is effectively no meaningful 52-week price history — this is a new listing, which is why the quantitative signals should be disregarded entirely. The stock has no valid 200-day moving average (the scan shows the 200-day and 50-day at essentially the same value, 141.81, which is an artefact of insufficient history rather than a real technical condition), no established base and no relative-strength track record. What history exists is a post-listing decline: from a high of 211.39 to 140.00, a fall of 33.8%, which is the ordinary unwinding of initial listing euphoria as the float expands rather than evidence of business deterioration. Price has repeatedly found a floor around 138-140.

critical.valuation: At 88.1x forward the market is paying a strategic premium for a genuinely unique asset, and no conventional valuation framework will make that look cheap. The honest assessment is that this is a business-quality and scarcity bet rather than a valuation or technical one — which is precisely why the WATCH rating rather than a buy signal, and why the quant score should be disregarded. The disciplined approach with a new listing of this profile is to let the float overhang clear and the first few quarters of disclosure accumulate before committing capital.
